name: Vitrake
numberNote: Personal field-guide number; not a National Pokédex number.
mechanicsTarget: Pokémon Scarlet and Violet / Generation IX (including DLC moves)
spriteTarget: Generation III visual style only; battle rules use Generation IX.
nameEtymology: Vitr- evokes glass and vitreous materials; drake supplies the dragon half. The name points to the clear horn reservoirs.
entries: The two liquids in its horns are harmless apart. When danger approaches, it mixes them inside its shell and fires a scorching burst from the dragon-shaped mouth.
Most foes flee at the sight of its dragon-faced shell. Even with empty horns, it stands its ground and hisses as loudly as it can.
description: A small beetle shelters beneath a red carapace shaped like a dragon's head. Two clear horns hold different liquids. Their contents meet in a chamber behind the shell's mouth, turning a convincing bluff into a powerful blast.

lore.behavior: Vitrake lifts the front of its shell before it fires. This warning display usually settles a quarrel, leaving its precious horn stores untouched. When the bluff fails, all six feet brace against the ground for a short, accurately aimed burst.
lore.personality: Proud and stubborn in a standoff, it becomes a busy, inquisitive little beetle around a trusted Trainer. After a successful warning display, it peeks out to check that everyone noticed.
lore.ecology: It searches damp leaf litter for small invertebrates and fallen berries, then rests beneath stones or fallen timber. A Vitrake returning to its shelter after a battle often has noticeably low liquid levels in its horns.
lore.refill: In this fictional species, feeding and rest replenish the two horn fluids. The horns are living transparent armor, not manufactured glass bottles.
lore.dragonIdentity: Its shell has the silhouette of a dragon's head, with paired horns, a heavy brow, and a blasting mouth. The insect's chemistry supplies the dragon's breath, and the intimidating face helps it avoid fights.
lore.realAnimal: Bombardier beetles use hot defensive spray from glands near the end of the abdomen, and can aim that spray precisely. Each of the paired glands has its own storage and reaction compartments.
lore.fictionBoundary: The transparent horns, one different fluid per horn, shared mouth chamber, dragon-shaped carapace, and front-facing outlet are invented for Vitrake. They are not the anatomy of a real bombardier beetle.

approvedFeatures: Six thoracic legs in three pairs
Two transparent horns, one on either side of the shell
Blue liquid in anatomical left horn
Amber liquid in anatomical right horn
Short broad shell mouth acts as chemical spitter
design.orientation: Left and right are the creature's own sides; front-facing views reverse those positions on the page.
design.sprayDirection: Forward through the shell's dragon mouth; the beetle turns and braces its body to aim.

abilities.name: Shell Armor
abilities.description: Prevents critical hits while the ability is active. Effects that ignore abilities can bypass it.

abilities.name: Mega Launcher
abilities.description: Multiplies the power of pulse moves by 1.5. Here it boosts Dragon Pulse, Water Pulse, and Dark Pulse; it does not boost Acid Spray, Bug Buzz, Flamethrower, Belch, or every move that looks like a blast.

typeMatchupsNote: Damage taken before Terastallization, items, abilities, weather, or other battle modifiers. Ground attacks still hit it; the shell does not grant levitation. Fire is neutral because Bug's weakness and Dragon's resistance cancel.

learnsetNote: All learn levels and access assignments belong to this fan species. All moves themselves exist under Scarlet/Violet rules. TM numbers are deliberately omitted; availability was checked using existing species' Gen IX TM sources.
battleRole: A sturdy special attacker that can soften a target with Acid Spray or attack immediately with pulse and sound moves. Its moderate Speed, five common weaknesses, limited four-move space, and lack of fast reliable recovery keep its strong attacks in check.

battleSet.name: Armored special attacker
battleSet.notes: A fan-format starting point, not a tournament recommendation. Boots cover its Stealth Rock weakness. Use the listed four moves; Water Pulse or Dark Pulse can replace one for different coverage. A 0 Attack IV reduces confusion and Foul Play damage.

balanceNotes: 520 BST is a normal fully developed nonlegendary total; existing comparisons include Clawitzer (500), Flygon (520), and Haxorus (540).
110 Special Attack and Mega Launcher make Dragon Pulse strong, but Fairy types are immune to it.
No Shell Smash, Quiver Dance, Nasty Plot, recovery such as Recover, or custom signature move is assigned. Rest is available with its normal sleep cost.
These are design checks, not a claim of competitive balance established by playtesting.
